# Lattice | Core QA User Guide

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Which organization is it best for? | Medium-sized enterprises of 100-1,000 people and large organizations requiring standardized talent management. |
| What is the primary problem it solves? | Its primary value is the AI-driven talent and performance platform, covering performance, objectives, participation, growth and remuneration. For the procurement party, this location should be mapped to quantifiable issues, such as data integrity, follow-up timeliness, scheduling time or evaluation completion. |
| Is it possible to replace the existing core system? | The replacement of the core HRIS depends on remuneration, statutory filing, master data and interface coverage. Not local HRIS/remuneration; TCO after seating and additional module; manual supervision of performance ratings and AI recommendations must be maintained. |
| How should AI and automation be evaluated? | Don't just watch the demo. Verify with 20—50 real records or one full cycle: input source, recommendation accuracy, manual review points, permissions, failure rollbacks, dosage costs, and audit records. |
| How do you understand public pricing? | Foundations $13/seat/month; separate Performance 10, Goals 8, Engineering 4; Compensation 6; Grow plus $4/sea/month; Enterprise request. The open price is only the software entrance, and taxes, minimum numbers, implementation, migration, integration, communications/AI usage and advanced support should enter the TCO for three years. |
| What should I pay attention to when using it in Hong Kong or across regions? | There is a need to verify labour rules, wage calculations, statutory forms, data presence and support time zones on a regional basis; “multi-country support” is not equivalent to a declaration of primary pay per country. |
| What are the integration priorities? | Priority checks for authentication, mail/calendar or attendance devices, master data direction, API limits, webhooks, error retries, field mappings, historical backfill, and delete synchronization. The "presence" of the interface does not mean that the real-time and governance requirements are met. |
| What is the typical implementation complexity? | Lightweight ranges can be imported and launched with standard templates first; once multi-entity, historical data, complex permissions, bi-directional integration, or statutory calculations are involved, design, cleaning, UAT, parallel operation, training, and post-launch support phases should be set up. |
| What is the minimum safety due diligence question? | Request the latest audit/certification, DPA, subcontractor list, data location, encryption, backup and recovery, RTO/RPO, SSO/SCIM, logs, deletion export mechanism, AI training policy and event notification terms. |
| Can the customer case directly prove the effect? | Official cases: Waterford is twice as fast, GoCardles has a participation rate ranging from 62 to 100 per cent and Agero has a 98 per cent completion rate. All of them are issued by the manufacturer and are subject to certification. The case can only prove a path of feasibility and cannot be a substitute for interviews with clients on the same scale, in the same area, with the modular POC. |
| What is the recommended POC? | Select a department or location to run a full cycle to validate employee data, clearance, time off/performance or recruitment; in the case of remuneration, complete at least one parallel pay and difference reconciliation. |
| When is it not recommended? | If critical requirements fall outside its boundaries, contract-level safety/compliance evidence cannot be provided, migration and exit scenarios are unclear, or three-year TCO is out of control with real usage, it is not advisable to procure solely because of the interface or AI demo. |
